questions.text:
A scientist is very interested in the SRY gene in humans, which is involved
in male sex  determination and which is never found on X chromosomes (i.e., this
gene occurs in the  "differential" region of the Y chromosome). SRY
is an example of a \_\_\_\_\_\_\_ gene."
Wei crosses a variegated (female) four-o\'clock with a green (male) pollen. What type(s) of plants will result from this cross?
In some traits, such as \_\_\_\_\_, phenotypes do not fall into distinct categories but are often heavily influenced by multiple genes collectively called \_\_\_\_\_.
The process by which somatic cells divide to increase their number is called:

The chi-square test is used to test the hypothesis--it is by chance and chance alone that the observed ratios fit the expected ratios from monohybrid and dihybrid crosses. When we apply this test, we should keep these notes in mind, except that:
choices: the probability (p) value from the test is the probability of observing a deviation from the expected results at least as large on the basis of chance if the hypothesis is correct.
the probability value p $>$ 0.05 means the hypothesis is true; whereas the probability value p $<$ 0.05 means the hypothesis is not true.
the probability value p $>$ 0.05 means that the results are compatible with that hypothesis.
the probability value p $<$ 0.05 means that the hypothesis has to be rejected.

questions.text: A disease that was made famous with its effects on the royal family was  hemophilia . Although it was passed on through all family members, the effects were seen only in male members. What type of trait is  hemophilia ?
During meiosis, \_\_\_\_\_ may either cross over by chance, producing recombinants, or not cross over at all, resulting in no recombinants being produced.
Obtaining a map of gene positions on the chromosomes is an  endeavor  that has occupied thousands of geneticists for the past 100 years. All of these are ways that gene maps are used, EXCEPT:
choices: allowing geneticists to isolate genes and discover their structure and function.
building genotypes for experimental purposes or for commercial applications.

questions.text:
In humans, oculocutaneous (OCA) albinism is a collection of autosomal recessive
conditions  characterized by an absence of the pigment melanin in skin, hair,
and eyes. That is,  pigmentation ($A$) is dominant over albino
characteristics ( $a$). For this question, assume the  phenotype
is determined by a single gene with two alleles.  If both biological parents have
melanin pigmentation, what are all of the possible genotypes  that may be observed
in their offspring?"

A young man's family is afflicted by red -green color blindness. He decides
to draw a  pedigree of his family detailing the inheritance of this condition,
and notices that \u2014in his  family\u2014only he and his grandfather demonstrate
red- green color blindness. Furthermore,  none of his aunts or uncles have this
condition, and his brother can distinguish between red and  green. Red-green color
blindness is most likely"
Using independent assortment, what percent of offspring will be  a;b + if the parents are  a;b + and a+;b?
During Mendel\'s experiments, the alleles that were visible in heterozygotes (i.e., that resulted in an observable phenotype, such as yellow seeds) were:

I n a certain species of sunflower, height is determined by 3 genes. In this particular species, the dominant allele contributes 3 doses of height. The recessive allele contributes 1 dose. An organism inherits 1 dominant allele and 1 recessive allele for each gene. How many doses of height does this organism receive?
A human disease appears to be associated with dysfunctional mitochondria, but actually  results from a mutation at a single locus in nuclear DNA. This mutation will demonstrate a
choices: maternal pattern of inheritance, because mitochondria are passed from female parents to
paternal pattern of inheritance, because mitochondria are passed from male parents to
non-Mendelian inheritance pattern, because the number of mitochondria varies from cell to
Mendelian inheritance pattern, as the mutation is located on an autosome.

questions.text: Which of these examples best represents variable expressivity?
choices: In a population of mice all having the genotype  G / g , half of the mice have gray coats and half have white coats.
In a population of mice all having the genotype  G / g , mice demonstrate coats ranging in color from light gray to very dark gray (almost black).
In a population of mice all having the genotype  G / g , all mice demonstrate coats of only one color (gray).
In a population of mice all having the genotype  G / g , all mice completely lack any pigmentation in their coats (i.e., have white coats).
None of the answer options demonstrate variable expressivity.

questions.text: Imagine you are a researcher attempting to identify the mutation responsible for an interesting phenotype in a hypothetical animal. You have obtained an F2 population from a sufficiently large cross of wildtype and mutant stocks and can access the DNA and genome sequence of your area of interest in any animal involved in your experiment. What else do you require to perform a combined linkage and physical map analysis to find the gene responsible and identify the causal mutation?
choices: a linkage map generated using polymorphisms that alter the visible phenotype
a list of densely packed molecular marker loci and associated linkage map in the area of interest
a physical map of the region of interest

questions.text:
Suppose a novel condition has been studied in several families and is known
to be caused by  a mutation in one gene. The given table shows families where the
condition is present. The four  rightmost columns record the number of offspring
in each family. Select the most likely mode of inheritance of the condition.

Satoshi is breeding tigers. He breeds an orange tiger with
a white tiger. All of their offspring are orange. He then
breeds their offspring and finds that there are
approximately three orange tiger babies for every one
white baby. Satoshi concludes that:
choices: orange color is a codominant trait in tigers.
orange color is an incompletely dominant trait in tigers.
orange color is a dominant trait in tigers.
orange color is a recessive trait in tigers

questions.text: Which of the following statements about molecular marker loci used in genetic linkage mapping is CORRECT?
choices: They directly identify a gene of interest.
They are regions of DNA that do not vary between individuals.
They typically consist of DNA that does not affect the viability of the organism.
They often separate from a gene of interest during recombination.

questions.text: Define a pedigree analysis.
choices: a historical review of a particular phenotype within a family
a prediction of possible diseases within a family
a genetic screening for a particular disease
analysis of an individual's predisposition for certain diseases
